## Purpose

This is the Next.js App Router tree: it owns the root HTML shell, fonts, and global providers
([layout.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/layout.tsx)), and every routable URL in the product â€” auth, dashboard, admin, workflow
launch/run, and handoff. Every page here is a thin entrypoint that authenticates via
`localStorage` token + `getToken()` and then delegates the real UI to `components/`;
**nothing else in the frontend imports from `app`** (`imported_by: []` â€” it is a leaf the
router mounts, not a library other modules build on).

## Shape

- [layout.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/layout.tsx) â€” root layout (server component): loads Manrope + Heebo fonts, sets
  `<html>`/`<body>`, mounts `SkillsHooksProvider` then `RunConnectionProvider` above
  `{children}` so the app-level SSE run stream survives route changes.

- `page.tsx` â€” `/`, server component, immediate `redirect("/login")`.

- [login/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/login/page.tsx) â€” `/login`, client, Cognito username/password entry plus explicit
  NEW_PASSWORD_REQUIRED, software/email-MFA, and factor-choice continuation states. On a
  completed challenge it routes the effective principal to `/admin` or `/dashboard`.

- [forgot-password/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/forgot-password/page.tsx) â€” `/forgot-password`, client, a two-step,
  non-enumerating Cognito reset flow. The UI surfaces the deployment-wide email-MFA recovery
  limitation returned by the backend rather than pretending a reset code was sent.

- [settings/security/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/settings/security/page.tsx) â€” `/settings/security`, client, TOTP enrollment and
  verification for the signed-in Cognito principal.

- [admin/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/admin/page.tsx) â€” `/admin`, client, invitation-only user creation plus list/search,
  tier/role changes, temporary reset, disable/enable, and delete lifecycle actions. It routes an
  `admin_mfa_required` response to enrollment/re-login rather than treating it as an ordinary
  authorization failure.

- [dashboard/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/dashboard/page.tsx) â€” `/dashboard`, client, the main authenticated surface: chat lane +
  workflow runs + SSE/WS stream handling, wraps everything in `DashboardLayout`. The
  `*.source.test.ts` / `*.fix201.test.ts` files alongside it are colocated unit tests, not
  routes.

- [workflow/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/workflow/page.tsx) â€” `/workflow`, client, standalone agent-pipeline view (`WorkflowView` +
  `AgentLibrary` slide-out).

- [workflow/create/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/workflow/create/page.tsx) â€” `/workflow/create`, client, the single unified
  deliverable-launch route; reads `?mode=prototype|ppt` and renders `LaunchWizard` inside a
  `Suspense` boundary (required because `useSearchParams` needs one).

- `handoff/[token]/page.tsx` â€” `/handoff/:token`, client, dynamic segment; thin wrapper that
  hands the token straight to `HandoffWorkflow` (`components/handoff`).

- [handoff/settings/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/handoff/settings/page.tsx) â€” `/handoff/settings`, client, standalone integrations
  settings page (`IntegrationsCard`); deliberately not under a `/settings` route so the whole
  handoff feature stays one route family.

- [preview-fullscreen/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/preview-fullscreen/page.tsx) â€” `/preview-fullscreen`, client, full-screen App Builder IDE
  opened via `window.open()` from `AppBuilderPreview`; reads the file payload out of
  `sessionStorage` rather than props/query, since the tab is a separate window.

- [test-preview/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/test-preview/page.tsx) â€” `/test-preview`, client, hardcoded `MOCK_FILES` harness for
  exercising `AppBuilderPreview` in isolation (dev/QA aid, not a product route).

- [admin/admin.reskin.test.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/admin/admin.reskin.test.tsx), [login/login.reskin.test.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/login/login.reskin.test.tsx) â€” colocated visual-reskin
  regression tests for their sibling pages.

Only `page.tsx` (root) and [layout.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/layout.tsx) are server components; every actual page is
`"use client"` because each one needs browser APIs on mount (`localStorage` token,
`useRouter`, `sessionStorage`, `window.location`). `RootLayout` is the sole place providers
are mounted â€” `SkillsHooksProvider` outside, `RunConnectionProvider` inside â€” so both are
live above every route in the tree, not per-page.

## Why this shape

The route segmentation mirrors the product's top-level nav (dashboard, workflow, admin,
handoff) one folder per surface, so the URL space is self-describing and each page can stay a
thin shell that imports its real implementation from `components/<feature>/`.

Only `/` is a redirect shim (`/` -> `/login`); the deleted `/register` route is not retained
because self-registration is not a supported Cognito path. `handoff/[token]` is the one dynamic
segment; it stays a one-line wrapper around `HandoffWorkflow` specifically so token-parsing logic
lives with the rest of the handoff feature, not duplicated at the route boundary.
`workflow/create` needs a `Suspense` boundary because `useSearchParams()` carries the mode
(prototype vs ppt) without a per-workflow route fork.

**The server/client split is minimal by necessity**: this is an authenticated-first app where
almost every route immediately needs `localStorage`/token state, so only the two routes with
no auth-dependent logic (root redirect, root layout) stay server components. The layout is
where the SSE run connection is deliberately hoisted above the router
(`RunConnectionProvider` wraps `{children}` in [layout.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/layout.tsx), not in [dashboard/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/dashboard/page.tsx)) â€”
that keeps a per-run stream alive across client-side navigations instead of being torn down
and reconnected on every route change.
